cost: THE ROUND NUMBER: dispatched as 217, FILED AS 220. data/rounds/217.json is already a landed round — players-to-team's recal_217, the DHO height floor / Draymond hub, on main at 75962d1 — and 216.json is players-to-team's recal_216 (the pnr handler gates). The receipts loader keys on the `round` field and warns that 'two round files both claim round N; <f> is the one that wins', i.e. a duplicate would silently shadow a landed receipt, so this round took the first number free of both the ledger and the in-flight batch (218 and 219 are the sibling o_score rounds). Renumbering it is a four-place edit: the section header in data/compute_ovr.py, two `round` fields plus the recal_N text in data/anchors.json, this file's name and `round`, and the commit subject.

ANDREW TONEY '81 IS NOT REACHED AND IT IS NOT A LOAD QUESTION. Asked 68 +-3, reads 73, unmoved. He played 23.6 mpg — 0.967 of LOAD_FULL, the 24-minute line recal_96 LOCATED from Clint Capela '17's pin rather than chose — so his paid volume is 79.27 against a raw 82 and his load factor goes 1.000 -> 0.971. His own arithmetic: clearance 23, z[2] 33, so the transfer is c x 23 + (c - 0.05) x 33 = 56c - 1.65, and he prints 71 (the top of his band) at o_score 76.87, i.e. at c <= 0.0927, i.e. at a load factor <= 0.713. NO reading of recal_96's share can deliver 0.713 to a man sitting at 0.967 — that is a proof, not a sweep. What he IS: a rookie shooting .535 TS in a .583 league with a BPM of -3.0, carrying an efficiency bar of 57 and a rim bar of 78 off the pre-1997 ZONE INFERENCE. That is an ATTRIBUTE complaint and it belongs to stats-to-ratings (build_ratings.py) — the same verdict round 196 reached for Dominique Wilkins '86.

THE FRONTIER THAT DOES REACH HIM, MEASURED ON THE WHOLE POOL AND PRICED, NOT TAKEN — HIS CALL. Read the transfer's load on recal_163's SECOND-payment minutes line instead of recal_96's: `a['volume'] x ramp(mpg, LOAD_FOOT, SECOND_FULL)`, 12 -> 33.9, on the argument that recal_196's own citation of recal_130 ('a rate paid twice is scaled twice') makes this the SECOND reading of the volume rate, and recal_130/163 settled that the second line is the class's upper quartile of minutes, not the bench boundary. IT LANDS ALL THREE SUBJECTS — Thompson 66, Toney 68, Williams 64 — HOLDS ALL 213 ANCHORS (0 failing) and keeps every full-load subject byte-identical INCLUDING Paul Westphal '80 at 32.5 mpg. ITS PRICE IS THE CLASS IT REPRICES: 306 cards move instead of 79 and 207 of them are between 24 and 33.9 mpg — Walter Davis '81 -6, Mike Woodson '82 -6 and '84 -6, Purvis Short '80 -6, James Silas '81 -6, Quintin Dailey '83 -6 and '85 -6, Albert King '84 -5, David Thompson '83 -5, Junior Bridgeman '81 -5, Freeman Williams '80/'81 -5, Andrew Toney '82 -5. Those men are not part-time scorers, they are rotation starters, and several sit in the post-84 class he called FINE in round 215. Cutting them is a ruling, not a repair.

notes: THE DEFECT IS A MISQUOTE OF THE LAW recal_196 ITSELF CITES. Its LOAD factor is documented as 'recal_131's own scoring-load line, PZ_V_LO/PZ_V_HI (volume 55 -> 80). recal_130's rule: a rate paid twice is scaled twice.' But recal_131's paint floor reads that line on `_vol` — the volume bar AFTER recal_96's minutes share — and recal_196 read the same two numbers on the RAW bar a['volume']. Same line, two different quantities, and the raw one is exactly what recal_96 was written to stop pricing: 'volume is a usage percentile, per possession he was on the floor for, and o_score never asked how much of a game the man was on the floor.'

WHAT IT COST, on the card that names the round. David Thompson '82, 20.4 mpg, load share 0.700. The vector pays his volume 87 as 60.90 and his playvol 42 as 29.40 — and then the era transfer read the SAME volume bar raw, 87, cleared the 80 at the top of the line and paid him load 1.000. Coefficient 0.13 x era 0.950 x creation 1.000 x load 1.000 = 0.1234, on a clearance of 56 capped at the pool's p95 of 52, plus recal_210's balance of 1.175: +7.594 of o_score, the largest single era transfer on the board, paid to a man the same function had just ruled a part-time scorer nine lines earlier.

THE FIX IS ONE SUBSTITUTION AND NO NEW NUMBER: `_vol` for `a['volume']`, on the same 55 -> 80 line. Thompson's load factor becomes 0.236, his coefficient 0.0291, his transfer +1.516 — and recal_210's balance falls to zero, because the coefficient is now under the third zone's own 0.05, which is the term's own statement that there is nothing left to transfer. He prints 68, the ruling's number exactly. Sly Williams '83 the same way: 20.4 mpg, share 0.700, transfer +5.300 -> +1.007, 69 -> 65, his number exactly.

IDENTITY AT FULL LOAD, BY CONSTRUCTION — this is why the protected list is byte-identical rather than merely close. `_vol = a['volume'] x load_share(p)` and load_share returns 1.0 for every card at or above LOAD_FULL (24 mpg) AND for every card with no minutes on the sheet (recal_52's rule), so `_vol == a['volume']` there. Gervin '80 (37.6), Kareem '80 (38.3), Jordan '87 (40.0), Westphal '80 (32.5), Bird '83 (37.7) and '84 (38.3), Drexler '88 (37.8), Hakeem '94 (41.0), Magic '90 (37.2), Ewing '90 (38.6), Moses '82 (42.0), Maxwell '80 (34.3), Isiah '85 (38.1), Stockton '90 (37.4), KJ '89 (39.2) and '92 (37.2), Dantley '84 (37.8), King '84 (34.6).

MEASURED ON THE WHOLE POOL, against the base board: 79 of 10,000 cards move on OFF, EVERY ONE OF THEM DOWN, max -7, mean -2.08; 62 move on OVR, max -5; DEF moves on ZERO cards and every attribute on ZERO (build_ratings.py is unchanged but for the version stamp — 0 cards differ on any attribute). Every mover is a 1980-1996 card and every mover's minutes lie between 16.1 and 23.8 — the class the ruling names, and nothing else. No 1997+ card moves on any scale. The top 12 by OFF is unchanged and no card enters or leaves the top 50 by OVR.

MONOTONE STILL (recal_210's law). The load factor reads no scoring bar, and the substitution can only SHRINK the coefficient c, so both derivatives survive unchanged in sign: below the clearance cap d(total)/dz[1] = 0.08 + c >= 0 and d(total)/dz[2] = max(0.05, c) - c >= 0. The regeneration's own zone-block monotonicity line prints 0 cards / 0 (card, bar) pairs, as it did at 210.

THE OTHER READING INSIDE THE RULING — the load factor reading recal_96's SHARE directly instead of the paid volume — was measured too: Thompson 71, Williams 67, Toney 73. It lands two of three at the very top edge of their bands instead of on their numbers, and it throws away the 55 -> 80 line recal_196 chose. The paid-volume reading is both the more faithful quote (recal_131 reads the line on exactly this quantity) and the closer fit, so it is the one taken.

WHY THE CREATION LEG WAS NOT THE ANSWER EITHER, since the ruling offered it as an alternative ('its creation test should not saturate at playvol 41 for a bench scorer'): Toney's playvol is 64 RAW and 61.87 PAID, so the test saturates on either quantity, and recomputing the 27 -> 41 line off the pool's paid-playvol distribution lowers it and saturates more cards, not fewer. The creation leg cannot cut a man who genuinely created his own looks; what is wrong with Toney '81 is the efficiency and zone bars, upstream.
